SubstrateMapE142BinCodeEntry.description: One sparse BinCode entry, for MapType Coordinate and Row/Column. $text carries the element's token content, which JSON has no other name for; the four attributes are the XSD's. LID.description: V0125 location id, xs:string with NO facet in the one revision that declares it - a LID is an opaque join key and is never normalized. Clause 13.3 addresses a position by the X/Y coordinate, the location identifier, or BOTH. A LID-only entry takes the next FREE cell in document order and is not reported; only when the lattice is full does it become unplaceable, and it is then excluded and reported once via E142_XML_LID_ONLY_EXCLUDED. It is retained in sparseBinCodes either way.

SubstrateMapE142BinCodeMap.description: E142 BinCodeMapType. BinCode carries the SAME token text the XML carries - the payload is normative and must survive the round trip byte-for-byte, so it is never serialized decoded. Its JSON shape is decided by MapType: 2DArray -> string[] (one row each); Array -> one string, row-major; Coordinate and Row/Column -> BinCodeEntry[]. EXACTLY ONE of BinCode and $binary must be present: they are two encodings of one payload, so neither is required on its own and carrying both is a defect. draft-04 cannot express "exactly one" over property PRESENCE without oneOf, which is what the two branches below do.

LayoutSpecifier.description: Path into Layouts. "" is the layoutless form and is a VALUE, not an absence. No xs:keyref covers it, so a dangling specifier warns and falls back to dimensions from the payload.

Orientation.description: Degrees, OrientationType facets 0..359. Out of range is an ERROR, not a tolerated value: clamping or normalizing would be a guess about which way the substrate physically sits.

Overlay.description: Overlays, in document order. minOccurs="0" in EVERY revision, so a SubstrateMap with NO overlay is legal and occurs in the corpus - the source substrates of a transfer chain carry none. maxOccurs="unbounded", so this is an array even with one entry. Which overlay to RENDER is the control's decision: no schema revision defines a default overlay.

SubstrateMapE142MapDataJson.description:
The SEMI E142.1 MapData document as JSON - one more input and output encoding for the engine's E142Document, not a second data model. Member names are the XSD's element and attribute names verbatim, PascalCase; GridData's are camelCase, and that case difference is the boundary between the two vocabularies. See Schema/E142/JSON-FORMAT.md, which is the contract this file encodes.

NOTE ON STRICTNESS: additionalProperties is false throughout, while parseE142Json warns about an unknown member and parses on. That is deliberate and matches GridData: the schema is the engineering-time contract and may be strict, the runtime parser reads other producers' documents and may never be stricter than the schema.

$format.description: Mandatory discriminator, and the FIRST member. A document whose first member is anything else is not an E142 JSON document. No GridData key is named $format, so the two are distinguishable without parsing either further.

$version.description: Mandatory. Versions THIS envelope, not SEMI's schema - that travels in $namespace. 1 is the token form; 2 adds the optional $binary payload member. A document should declare the LOWEST version whose features it uses, so a version-1 reader is not refused a document it could read.

$namespace.description: The E142.1 namespace URI verbatim, so a round trip reproduces it instead of promoting every document to V0125. Absent means the serializer default.

Layouts.description: The layout tree. LayoutId is unique across the document.

SubstrateMaps.description: The maps. (SubstrateType, SubstrateId, LayoutSpecifier) is unique. minOccurs="0" in EVERY revision, like Layouts and Substrates - SEMI's own BinCodeMap-Extension-Example carries Substrates and nothing else, so a MapData with no map at all is legal and occurs in the corpus.

SubstrateMapE142BinaryPayload.description: A payload as bin indices. An ENCODING of the token text, expanded back to BinCode before anything else reads the document, so it can mean nothing the token form cannot. See JSON-FORMAT.md.

Codes.description: The code table IN INDEX ORDER; Codes[0] is the null bin. Index i means Codes[i], so re-sorting renumbers every cell.

Data.description: Base64 of little-endian uint16 cell indices, row-major.

Cols.description: Lattice columns. Stated because an index stream cannot say where a row ends.
